sanskrit: ahaṃ te dayitaṃ putraṃ pretarājavaśaṃ gatam punar dāsyāmi tad rūpaṃ mā śucaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: "Your beloved son, gone into the power of the Lord of the Dead, I shall give back to you in that very form. Do not grieve, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu nṛpatiṃ prayātau svo yathepsitam sṛñjayaś ca yathākāmaṃ praviveśa svamandiram
english: Having spoken thus to the king, we two departed as we had wished; and Sṛñjaya, his desire fulfilled, entered his own palace.

sanskrit: sṛñjayasyātha rājarṣeḥ kasmiṃś cit kālaparyaye jajñe putro mahāvīryas tejasā prajvalann iva
english: Then to Sṛñjaya, the royal sage, in the course of time, was born a son of mighty valor, blazing as it were with splendor.

sanskrit: vavṛdhe sa yathākālaṃ sarasīva mahotpalam babhūva kāñcanaṣṭhīvī yathārthaṃ nāma tasya tat
english: He grew in due season like a great lotus in a lake, and he became Golden-Spittle: rightly did that name belong to him.

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ loke paprathe kurusattama bubudhe tac ca devendro varadānaṃ mahātmanoḥ
english: That most wondrous thing spread through the world, O best of the Kurus; and the lord of the gods came to know of the boon granted by the two great-souled ones.

sanskrit: tatas tv abhibhavād bhīto bṛhaspatimate sthitaḥ kumārasyāntaraprekṣī babhūva balavṛtrahā
english: Then the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, fearing to be overthrown, took his stand upon the counsel of Bṛhaspati and lay in wait for an opening against the boy.

sanskrit: codayām āsa vajraṃ sa divyāstraṃ mūrtisaṃsthitam vyāghro bhūtvā jahīmaṃ tvaṃ rājaputram iti prabho
english: He charged the thunderbolt, that divine weapon embodied in form: "Become a tiger and slay this prince!" — so he commanded, O lord.

sanskrit: vivṛddhaḥ kila vīryeṇa mām eṣo 'bhibhaviṣyati sṛñjayasya suto vajra yathainaṃ parvato dadau
english: "Grown great in might, this one will surely overthrow me, O thunderbolt — this son of Sṛñjaya, even as Parvata bestowed him."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu śakreṇa vajraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ kumārasyāntaraprekṣī nityam evānvapadyata
english: Thus addressed by Śakra, the thunderbolt, conqueror of hostile cities, continually followed the boy, watching for an opening.

sanskrit: sṛñjayo 'pi sutaṃ prāpya devarājasamadyutim hṛṣṭaḥ sāntaḥpuro rājā vananityo 'bhavat tadā
english: And Sṛñjaya, having gained a son radiant as the king of the gods, the king rejoiced; and then, with his harem, he took to dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: tato bhāgīrathītīre kadā cid vananirjhare dhātrīdvitīyo bālaḥ sa krīḍārthaṃ paryadhāvata
english: Then once, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, by a forest stream, the child ran about at play, his nurse beside him.

sanskrit: pañcavarṣakadeśīyo bālo nāgendravikramaḥ sahasotpatitaṃ vyāghram āsasāda mahābalaḥ
english: The boy, about five years of age, with the prowess of a lordly elephant, in his great strength came upon a tiger that had sprung up all at once.

sanskrit: tena caiva viniṣpiṣṭo vepamāno nṛpātmajaḥ vyasuḥ papāta medinyāṃ tato dhātrī vicukruśe
english: Crushed by it, the king's son, trembling, fell lifeless to the earth; and at that the nurse cried out in anguish.

sanskrit: hatvā tu rājaputraṃ sa tatraivāntaradhīyata śārdūlo devarājasya māyayāntarhitas tadā
english: And having slain the prince, that tiger vanished on the very spot, made to disappear then by the magic of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: dhātryās tu ninadaṃ śrutvā rudatyāḥ paramārtavat abhyadhāvata taṃ deśaṃ svayam eva mahīpatiḥ
english: Hearing the cry of the nurse as she wept in utmost distress, the lord of the earth himself ran to that place.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa gatāsuṃ taṃ śayānaṃ pītaśoṇitam kumāraṃ vigatānandaṃ niśākaram iva cyutam
english: He beheld the boy lying lifeless, his blood drained, robbed of all joy, like the moon fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: sa tam utsaṅgam āropya paripīḍitavakṣasam putraṃ rudhirasaṃsiktaṃ paryadevayad āturaḥ
english: Lifting onto his lap that son with the crushed chest, drenched in blood, he lamented over him in his anguish.

sanskrit: tatas tā mātaras tasya rudantyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ abhyadhāvanta taṃ deśaṃ yatra rājā sa sṛñjayaḥ
english: Then the mothers of the boy, weeping, wasted with grief, ran to that place where King Sṛñjaya was.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā sasmāra mām antargatamānasaḥ tac cāhaṃ cintitaṃ jñātvā gatavāṃs tasya darśanam
english: Then the king, his mind turned inward, called me to mind; and I, knowing that he had thus thought of me, came into his sight.

sanskrit: sa mayaitāni vākyāni śrāvitaḥ śokalālasaḥ yāni te yaduvīreṇa kathitāni mahīpate
english: Lost in grief, he was made to hear from me these very words which the hero of the Yadus has told to you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: saṃjīvitaś cāpi mayā vāsavānumate tadā bhavitavyaṃ tathā tac ca na tac chakyam ato 'nyathā
english: And the boy was restored to life by me then, with Vāsava's consent; for what is destined must be so, and it cannot be otherwise than that.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ kumāraḥ sa svarṇaṣṭhīvī mahāyaśāḥ cittaṃ prasādayām āsa pitur mātuś ca vīryavān
english: Thereafter the prince Golden-Spittle, of great renown and valor, gladdened the hearts of his father and his mother.

sanskrit: kārayām āsa rājyaṃ sa pitari svargate vibhuḥ varṣāṇām ekaśatavat sahasraṃ bhīmavikramaḥ
english: When his father had gone to heaven, that mighty one of terrible prowess ruled the kingdom for a thousand and a hundred years.

sanskrit: tata iṣṭvā mahāyajñair bahubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ tarpayām āsa devāṃś ca pitṝṃś caiva mahādyutiḥ
english: Then, having performed many great sacrifices with abundant priestly gifts, that one of great splendor satisfied both the gods and the ancestors.

sanskrit: utpādya ca bahūn putrān kulasaṃtānakāriṇaḥ kālena mahatā rājan kāladharmam upeyivān
english: And having begotten many sons to continue the line, in the fullness of long time, O king, he came to the law of Time.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ rājendra saṃjātaṃ śokam etan nivartaya yathā tvāṃ keśavaḥ prāha vyāsaś ca sumahātapāḥ
english: So you, O lord of kings, turn back this grief that has arisen within you, even as Keśava and Vyāsa of mighty austerity have counseled you.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyam āsthāya duram udvaha iṣṭvā puṇyair mahāyajñair iṣṭāṃl lokān avāpsyasi
english: Take up the kingdom of your fathers and forefathers, and bear hard the burden of rule; and by performing holy great sacrifices you shall attain the worlds you desire.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ tu rājānaṃ śocamānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram tapasvī dharmatattvajñaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To the king Yudhiṣṭhira, fallen silent and grieving, the ascetic Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, knower of the truth of dharma, then spoke.

sanskrit: prajānāṃ pālanaṃ dharmo rājñāṃ rājīvalocana dharmaḥ pramāṇaṃ lokasya nityaṃ dharmānuvartanam
english: "The protection of subjects is the dharma of kings, O lotus-eyed one. Dharma is the standard of the world, and constant conformity to dharma is the rule."

sanskrit: anutiṣṭhasva vai rājan pitṛpaitāmahaṃ padam brāhmaṇeṣu ca yo dharmaḥ sa nityo vedaniścitaḥ
english: "Hold fast, O king, to the station of your fathers and forefathers; and the dharma that lies among the brāhmaṇas is eternal, established by the Veda."

sanskrit: tat pramāṇaṃ pramāṇānāṃ śāśvataṃ bharatarṣabha tasya dharmasya kṛtsnasya kṣatriyaḥ parirakṣitā
english: "That is the standard of standards, everlasting, O bull of the Bharatas; and of that dharma in its entirety the kṣatriya is the protector."

sanskrit: tathā yaḥ pratihanty asya śāsanaṃ viṣaye naraḥ sa bāhubhyāṃ vinigrāhyo lokayātrāvighātakaḥ
english: "And whatever man within his realm strikes against his command, that wrecker of the world's course is to be restrained by force of arms."

sanskrit: pramāṇam apramāṇaṃ yaḥ kuryān mohavaśaṃ gataḥ bhṛtyo vā yadi vā putras tapasvī vāpi kaś cana pāpān sarvair upāyais tān niyacched ghātayeta vā
english: "Whoever, fallen under the sway of delusion, makes the standard no standard — be he a servant, or a son, or even some ascetic — those wicked ones the king should restrain by every means, or put to death."

sanskrit: ato 'nyathā vartamāno rājā prāpnoti kilbiṣam dharmaṃ vinaśyamānaṃ hi yo na rakṣet sa dharmahā
english: "A king who acts otherwise than this incurs guilt; for he who does not guard dharma when it is perishing is himself a slayer of dharma."

sanskrit: te tvayā dharmahantāro nihatāḥ sapadānugāḥ svadharme vartamānas tvaṃ kiṃ nu śocasi pāṇḍava rājā hi hanyād dadyāc ca prajā rakṣec ca dharmataḥ
english: "Those slayers of dharma were struck down by you, together with their followers. Acting in your own dharma, why then do you grieve, O Pāṇḍava? For a king must slay, must give, and must protect his subjects according to dharma."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na te 'bhiśaṅke vacanaṃ yad bravīṣi tapodhana aparokṣo hi te dharmaḥ sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "I do not doubt the word you speak, O treasury of austerity; for dharma is no hidden thing to you, O best of all upholders of dharma."

sanskrit: mayā hy avadhyā bahavo ghātitā rājyakāraṇāt tāny akāryāṇi me brahman dahanti ca tapanti ca
english: "Yet many who ought not to have been slain were slain by me for the sake of the kingdom; those things I ought not to have done, O brahmin, sear me and burn me."

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca īśvaro vā bhavet kartā puruṣo vāpi bhārata haṭho vā vartate loke karmajaṃ vā phalaṃ smṛtam
english: Vyāsa said: "Either God may be the doer, O Bhārata, or the individual man, or chance prevails in the world, or the fruit is held to be born of action."

sanskrit: īśvareṇa niyuktā hi sādhv asādhu ca pārthiva kurvanti puruṣāḥ karma phalam īśvaragāmi tat
english: "If men, appointed by God, perform their deeds both good and ill, O lord of earth, then that fruit goes to God."

sanskrit: yathā hi puruṣaś chindyād vṛkṣaṃ paraśunā vane chettur eva bhavet pāpaṃ paraśor na kathaṃ cana
english: "For just as a man may fell a tree with an axe in the forest, the guilt would belong to the feller, and in no way to the axe."

sanskrit: atha vā tad upādānāt prāpnuyuḥ karmaṇaḥ phalam daṇḍaśastrakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ puruṣe tan na vidyate
english: "Or if men were to gain the fruit of the deed because they took up the means, still the guilt wrought by rod and sword would not be found in the man."

sanskrit: na caitad iṣṭaṃ kaunteya yad anyena phalaṃ kṛtam prāpnuyād iti tasmāc ca īśvare tan niveśaya
english: "And this is not held to be right, O son of Kuntī — that one should reap the fruit of what another has wrought. Therefore lay it upon God."

sanskrit: atha vā puruṣaḥ kartā karmaṇoḥ śubhapāpayoḥ na paraṃ vidyate tasmād evam anyac chubhaṃ kuru
english: "Or if the man is the doer of his deeds, both fair and foul, and no other agent is found, then in that case do some other good."

sanskrit: na hi kaś cit kva cid rājan diṣṭāt pratinivartate daṇḍaśastrakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ puruṣe tan na vidyate
english: "For no one anywhere, O king, can turn back from what is destined; and the guilt wrought by rod and sword is not found in the man."

sanskrit: yadi vā manyase rājan haṭhe lokaṃ pratiṣṭhitam evam apy aśubhaṃ karma na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
english: "Or if you think, O king, that the world rests upon chance, then in that case too the evil deed has neither been nor shall be."

sanskrit: athābhipattir lokasya kartavyā śubhapāpayoḥ abhipannatamaṃ loke rājñām udyatadaṇḍanam
english: "But if responsibility for good and evil must be assigned to the world, then the most fitting thing in the world is the lifted rod of kings."

sanskrit: athāpi loke karmāṇi samāvartanta bhārata śubhāśubhaphalaṃ ceme prāpnuvantīti me matiḥ
english: "And again, if deeds come round full circle in the world, O Bhārata, then these men reap the fruit, fair and foul, of their own doing — such is my view."

sanskrit: evaṃ satyaṃ śubhādeśaṃ karmaṇas tat phalaṃ dhruvam tyaja tad rājaśārdūla maivaṃ śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Thus, true and yielding good counsel, is the certain fruit of action. Cast it off, O tiger among kings; do not set your mind on grief in this way."

sanskrit: svadharme vartamānasya sāpavāde 'pi bhārata evam ātmaparityāgas tava rājan na śobhanaḥ
english: "For one acting in his own dharma, even when there is reproach, O Bhārata, this abandonment of self, O king, is unbecoming of you."

sanskrit: vihitānīha kaunteya prāyaścittāni karmiṇām śarīravāṃs tāni kuryād aśarīraḥ parābhavet
english: "Atonements are ordained here for the doers of deeds, O son of Kuntī; one possessed of a body may perform them, but the bodiless would meet ruin."

sanskrit: tad rājañ jīvamānas tvaṃ prāyaścittaṃ cariṣyasi prāyaścittam akṛtvā tu pretya taptāsi bhārata
english: "Therefore, O king, while you yet live, you shall perform the atonement; but if you do not make atonement, you shall burn for it hereafter, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hatāḥ putrāś ca pautrāś ca bhrātaraḥ pitaras tathā śvaśurā guravaś caiva mātulāḥ sapitāmahāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Slain are sons and grandsons, brothers and fathers too, fathers-in-law, teachers, maternal uncles, together with grandfathers."

sanskrit: kṣatriyāś ca mahātmānaḥ saṃbandhisuhṛdas tathā vayasyā jñātayaś caiva bhrātaraś ca pitāmaha
english: "And great-souled kṣatriyas, kinsmen and friends alike, companions and relatives and brothers, O grandfather —"

sanskrit: bahavaś ca manuṣyendrā nānādeśasamāgatāḥ ghātitā rājyalubdhena mayaikena pitāmaha
english: "and many lords of men, gathered from diverse lands — all were brought to death by me alone, greedy for the kingdom, O grandfather."

sanskrit: tāṃs tādṛśān ahaṃ hatvā dharmanityān mahīkṣitaḥ asakṛt somapān vīrān kiṃ prāpsyāmi tapodhana
english: "Having slain such men as those — guardians of the earth, ever steadfast in dharma, heroes who again and again drank the soma — what shall I attain, O treasury of austerity?"

sanskrit: dahyāmy aniśam adyāhaṃ cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ hīnāṃ pārthivasiṃhais taiḥ śrīmadbhiḥ pṛthivīm imām
english: "Day and night now I burn, brooding again and again upon this earth, bereft of those lordly lions among kings in all their splendor."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā jñātivadhaṃ ghoraṃ hatāṃś ca śataśaḥ parān koṭiśaś ca narān anyān paritapye pitāmaha
english: "Beholding the terrible slaughter of kinsmen, enemies slain by the hundred and other men by the millions, I am consumed with anguish, O grandfather."

sanskrit: kā nu tāsāṃ varastrīṇām avasthādya bhaviṣyati vihīnānāṃ svatanayaiḥ patibhir bhrātṛbhis tathā
english: "What now shall be the lot of those noble women, bereft of their own sons, their husbands, and their brothers?"

sanskrit: asmān antakarān ghorān pāṇḍavān vṛṣṇisaṃhitān ākrośantyaḥ kṛśā dīnā nipatantyaś ca bhūtale
english: "Reviling us — the dreadful Pāṇḍavas, bringers of the end, leagued with the Vṛṣṇis — gaunt and wretched, falling down upon the ground,"

sanskrit: apaśyantyaḥ pitṝn bhrātṝn patīn putrāṃś ca yoṣitaḥ tyaktvā prāṇān priyān sarvā gamiṣyanti yamakṣayam
english: "those women, seeing no more their fathers, brothers, husbands, and sons, will all give up their dear lives and go to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: vatsalatvād dvijaśreṣṭha tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ vyaktaṃ saukṣmyāc ca dharmasya prāpsyāmaḥ strīvadhaṃ vayam
english: "Of this I have no doubt, O best of the twice-born: through their tender love, and clearly through the subtlety of dharma, we shall incur the slaughter of women as well."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ suhṛdo hatvā kṛtvā pāpam anantakam narake nipatiṣyāmo hy adhaḥśirasa eva ca
english: "We, having slain our friends and wrought sin without end, shall fall headlong into hell, head downward indeed."

sanskrit: śarīrāṇi vimokṣyāmas tapasogreṇa sattama āśramāṃś ca viśeṣāṃs tvaṃ mamācakṣva pitāmaha
english: "We shall cast off our bodies by fierce austerity, O most virtuous one. Declare to me, O grandfather, the several modes of holy life."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhirasya tad vākyaṃ śrutvā dvaipāyanas tadā samīkṣya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā ṛṣiḥ provāca pāṇḍavam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that speech of Yudhiṣṭhira, the seer Dvaipāyana then, pondering it keenly with his intellect, spoke to the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā rājan kṣatradharmam anusmara svadharmeṇa hatā hy ete kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: "Do not give way to despair, O king; recall the dharma of the warrior. By their own dharma these kṣatriyas were slain, O bull among kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: kāṅkṣamāṇāḥ śriyaṃ kṛtsnāṃ pṛthivyāṃ ca mahad yaśaḥ kṛtāntavidhisaṃyuktāḥ kālena nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Coveting sovereignty entire and great glory upon the earth, bound by the ordinance of fate, they went to their destruction through Time."

sanskrit: na tvaṃ hantā na bhīmo 'pi nārjuno na yamāv api kālaḥ paryāyadharmeṇa prāṇān ādatta dehinām
english: "Not you are the slayer, nor Bhīma, nor Arjuna, nor the twins; it is Time that, by the law of succession, takes the life-breaths of embodied beings."

sanskrit: na yasya mātāpitarau nānugrāhyo 'sti kaś cana karmasākṣī prajānāṃ yas tena kālena saṃhṛtāḥ
english: "By that Time were they gathered in — Time, which has neither mother nor father, which has no one to favor, which is the witness of creatures' deeds."

sanskrit: hetumātram idaṃ tasya kālasya puruṣarṣabha yad dhanti bhūtair bhūtāni tad asmai rūpam aiśvaram
english: "This is but the instrument of that Time, O bull among men: that it slays beings by means of beings — that is its sovereign form."

sanskrit: karmamūrtyātmakaṃ viddhi sākṣiṇaṃ śubhapāpayoḥ sukhaduḥkhaguṇodarkaṃ kālaṃ kālaphalapradam
english: "Know Time to be the very embodiment of action, the witness of good and evil, whose outcome is the qualities of pleasure and pain, the bestower of the fruit of Time."

sanskrit: teṣām api mahābāho karmāṇi paricintaya vināśahetukāritve yais te kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Consider too, O mighty-armed one, the deeds of those men, by reason of which, as causes of their own destruction, they fell into the power of Time."

sanskrit: ātmanaś ca vijānīhi niyamavrataśīlatām yadā tvam īdṛśaṃ karma vidhinākramya kāritaḥ
english: "And recognize your own disposition toward restraint and vow and virtuous conduct, even when you were made to do such a deed, constrained by ordinance."

sanskrit: tvaṣṭreva vihitaṃ yantraṃ yathā sthāpayitur vaśe karmaṇā kālayuktena tathedaṃ bhrāmyate jagat
english: "As a contrivance fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ lies in the power of him who set it, so by action joined with Time is this world set whirling."

sanskrit: puruṣasya hi dṛṣṭvemām utpattim animittataḥ yadṛcchayā vināśaṃ ca śokaharṣāv anarthakau
english: "For seeing this coming-to-be of a man without apparent cause, and his perishing by mere chance, grief and joy are alike of no avail."

sanskrit: vyalīkaṃ cāpi yat tv atra cittavaitaṃsikaṃ tava tadartham iṣyate rājan prāyaścittaṃ tad ācara
english: "Yet whatever falsehood here ensnares your mind, for the sake of that, O king, atonement is enjoined: perform it."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca śrūyate pārtha yuddhe devāsure purā asurā bhrātaro jyeṣṭhā devāś cāpi yavīyasaḥ
english: "And this is heard, O Pārtha, of the war of gods and asuras of old: the asuras were the elder brothers, and the gods the younger."

sanskrit: teṣām api śrīnimittaṃ mahān āsīt samucchrayaḥ yuddhaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi dvātriṃśad abhavat kila
english: "Among them too, for the sake of sovereignty, there arose a great upheaval; the war lasted, it is said, two and thirty thousand years."

sanskrit: ekārṇavāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā rudhireṇa pariplutām jaghnur daityāṃs tadā devās tridivaṃ caiva lebhire
english: "Making the earth one ocean, awash with blood, the gods then slew the daityas and won for themselves the triple heaven."

sanskrit: tathaiva pṛthivīṃ labdhvā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ saṃśritā dānavānāṃ vai sāhyārthe darpamohitāḥ
english: "Even so, having gained the earth, brāhmaṇas versed to the end in the Vedas, deluded by pride, attached themselves to the aid of the dānavas."

sanskrit: śālāvṛkā iti khyātās triṣu lokeṣu bhārata aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi te cāpi vibudhair hatāḥ
english: "Renowned as the Śālāvṛkas throughout the three worlds, O Bhārata, those eighty-eight thousand too were slain by the gods."
